newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada regrets Deng's death but feelings mixed.
newsitem.headline: Canada regrets Deng's death but feelings mixed.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien expressed regret over the death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping on Wednesday but said feelings were mixed because of his record on human rights.

Asked by reporters to comment on Deng's actions in opening China up but also ordering tanks into Tiananmen Square in 1989 to crush pro-democracy demonstrations, Chretien said: "There's always mixed feelings on that situation.
"That's why whenever we meet with the leaders of China we always mention the rule of law."
Chretien drew fire from human rights activists for embracing Chinese Prime Minister Li Peng and trying to put a red bow of friendship on his head during a trade mission to China in November.
Chretien told reporters on Wednesday: "The question of human rights is always a problem of concern when we deal with them.
"But we have to recognise that this leader has opened his country to a new way closer to the western world, and (to be) more of a trading nation."
In an official statement, Chretien said: "We are confident that in the future China will continue to follow the path of reform and openness embarked upon by Deng."
